title: How a massive solar superstorm could end modern society
description: A step-by-step scientific breakdown of what would actually happen if a Carrington-class solar superstorm struck our modern world today.

shots.narration: A giant solar superstorm from the Sun threatens to destroy our modern world.
Deep inside, twisted magnetic fields trap energy equal to billions of exploding hydrogen bombs.
If the Sun were a basketball, Earth is just a tiny plastic bead.
In 1859, a massive white flare erupted and shot billions of tons of plasma.
This superheated cloud raced through space at two thousand kilometers per second.
It crossed the huge cosmic gulf to reach Earth in just eighteen hours.
The plasma slammed into our magnetic shield with terrifying kinetic force.
The impact squeezed our magnetic shield down by sixty thousand kilometers.
Brilliant green lights filled the night sky, waking people up at midnight.
The intense glow was bright enough to read a newspaper by.
Electric currents surged through telegraph wires, shocking the operators' hands.
Sparks flew from the machines and set telegraph paper on fire.
Today, our global power grids carry hundreds of thousands of volts.
A similar storm would send massive currents surging deep into the ground.
Within minutes, giant power transformers would heat up past three hundred degrees.
The heavy metal coils inside would melt like wax in an oven.
Replacing these custom machines takes up to two years of hard work.
Satellites in orbit would fall as the heated atmosphere drags them down.
Hundreds of millions of people would lose electricity for many months.
In 2012, a massive superstorm missed Earth by only nine days.
There is a twelve percent chance this disaster strikes this decade.
Without power, clean water would stop flowing to your thirsty throat.
A giant solar superstorm from the Sun threatens to destroy our modern world.
